newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela electric rate hikes approved. [CORRECTED 19:05 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela electric rate hikes approved. [CORRECTED 19:05 gmt]

text.p: Venezuela's state electricity generator and supplier EDELCA has been awarded a 20 percent increase in its tariffs, Venezuela's Official Gazette said. (Corrects to say that rate hikes were approved, though the 20 percent increase was granted to EDELCA).

According to the Gazette, in which all government decrees and resolutions are published, private utility Electricidad de Caracas will also receive a series of rate hikes every month for six months from July 1. (Clarifies that Electricidad de Caracas will also receive rate increases).

The Gazette did not give a percentage increase for the Electricidad de Caracas tariffs, but traders and analysts who saw the resolution said it was equivalent to more than 50 percent over the six months.
"It's great for Electricidad. It's much more than I would have expected," one analyst said.
Electricidad officials could not be reached for comment.
The initial 20 percent rate hike for EDELCA was back dated to May 30, the Gazette said.
Electric utilities have been demanding an increase in tariffs to cover higher costs since the start of the year and were hoping for an increase of between 40 and 45 percent.
At about 1315 local time/1715 GMT, Electricidad de Caracas shares rallied 37.00 bolivars to 686.00 bolivars.
